recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Syntho Field", "body": "Topher describes what he calls a syntho field, an idea he says he tested against Eileen McCusick and writes about on his Substack: just as a living body carries a biofield, certain surveillance and data-gathering programs have grown coherent enough that he perceives them as carrying a field of their own. Chance takes the hermetic route into it, arguing that if a biofield is simply information held in coherent flow, then systems reaching that level of complexity qualify by definition. Both frame it as something to be educated about rather than frightened by, and both stress that naming it is not the same as being victimized by it."}, {"title": "Suggestion Before Thought", "body": "The familiar moment when an ad appears for the exact thing you were just thinking about gets reversed here. Topher, citing conversations with Chris Crutchfield and Sabrina Wallace, argues the device does not read the thought so much as seed it first, then mirror it back, and that a coming credit and tokenomics economy built on securitized biometrics gives someone an incentive to provoke a measurable cortisol spike on cue. Chance pushes back by keeping room for premonition and presentiment, and jokes that when it happens to him he simply decides he is psychic, because that story sits better with his ego."}, {"title": "Desire, Boundaries, and Jurisdiction", "body": "Chance describes the co-opted desire faculty he meets constantly in biofield work, where people cannot locate anything they actually want, and calls desire the current in the river of abundance: block it and the flow drops to a trickle. They read Crowley's true will line as alignment with the creator's will rather than license, and land on the cleaner formulation that what is best for me is what is best for everyone. Topher balances the cosmic view with the human one, insisting boundaries matter, evil is whatever crosses one without permission, and there will always be invading hordes to hold a line against."}, {"title": "Language That Will Not Fit the Timeline", "body": "Chance argues the mainstream chronology strains against how ordinary people actually speak, since you can control printed books but not the tongue of illiterate country folk. He calls proto-Indo-European a construct with no artifact or inscription behind it, propped up to hold a Renaissance-era story together, and screen-shares a list of Celtic, Sanskrit and Latin cognates, walking through focal, vac and vox to show how mouth position turns one sound into another. Topher comes at it through architecture, which he calls frozen music and the least fakeable evidence, pointing to cyclopean stonework from Peru to China and Etruscan artifacts scattered across Europe and North Africa."}, {"title": "Fomenko's Graphs and the Cipher Question", "body": "The revised chronology of Russian mathematician Anatoly Fomenko is a fringe position, and the two treat it as an argument worth examining rather than settled fact. Chance highlights the Almagest analysis, which claims Ptolemy's star coordinates back-calculate to medieval skies, and walks through a dynasty graph pairing two Roman empires whose reign lengths match segment for segment until a joint rule diverges. He credits Michael Anthony Alberta with the speculative leap that such precision reads as encryption rather than laziness, and pitches an unclaimed project: use large language models to brute force the key nobody has."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: In this deep and dynamic conversation between Chance Garton (InnerVerse) and Topher Gardner (BioCharisma), the hidden architecture of mind and matter unfolds, from the spiritual implications of AI to the linguistic evidence of a forged historical timeline.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Exploring Fomenko’s New Chronology, the “synth field” of cybernetic consciousness, and the metaphysical battle between authentic will and implanted desire, this episode bridges philosophy, philology, and spiritual sovereignty.
